summary: Each 90s season loosely adapts one manga arc in our 1-60 unified act numbering (Dark Kingdom 1-14 / eps 1-46; Black Moon 15-26 / eps 60-88 after the anime-original Makai Tree eps 47-59; Infinity 27-38 / eps 90-127; Dream 39-49 / eps 128-166; Stars 50-60 / eps 173-200 after the anime-original Nehelenia-revival eps 167-172). No source anywhere carries per-episode chapter fields for this show - the adaptation borrows landmark beats and pads everything else, so the deliverable is a 37-anchor checkpoint lattice (arc boundaries + landmark beats), dense annotations for the anime-original devices (Rainbow Crystals, breakup subplot, pure-heart/talisman quest, dream-mirror hunts, Animamates-of-the-week), and a type correction: eps 167-172 are anime-original, not manga canon as AFL claims. STRUCTURE VERDICT: chapter-level interpolation between checkpoints is unreliable mid-season for this title; treat the mapping as arc-faithful checkpoints over a loose-parallel adaptation, not act-by-act coverage.

anchors.note: Near-faithful premiere: Usagi meets Luna, becomes Sailor Moon, Morga-as-Naru's-mother fight = Act 1 beat for beat.
Ami intro + Jadeite's brainwashing Crystal Seminar cram school = Act 2 exactly.
Rei/Hikawa Shrine + the disappearance bus = Act 3 exactly.
Princess party, Usagi's dress + first kiss with drunk Usagi = Act 4 Masquerade Dance Party, loosely staged.
Makoto transfers in and joins = Act 5; anime wraps it in the anime-original Rainbow Crystal device.
Sailor Venus debuts saving the Guardians, Tuxedo Mask gravely injured = Act 7 ending into Act 8; anime staging differs (Zoisite's fake Sailor Moon trap).
Usagi revealed as Princess Serenity when Tuxedo Mask falls = Act 9's central beat in both.
Past-life memories + Luna/Artemis exposition = Act 10 content; the Moon-ruins visit itself is deferred to ep 44 (rearranged).

anchors.chapters_adapted: 10 (Moon Kingdom ruins + Queen Serenity's message; rearranged)
anchors.note: The Guardians visit the ruined Moon Kingdom and meet Queen Serenity's spirit = Act 10's signature scene, relocated to the season endgame.
D Point final assault parallels Act 12 (Enemy - Queen Metaria); the four Guardians' on-screen deaths are anime-original staging.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 12-13 (heavily altered: Beryl/Metalia destroyed, reincarnation), 14 (daily-life reset echoed)
anchors.note: Season finale = Acts 12-13's final battle + rebirth, minus the manga's Usagi-kills-Mamoru-and-herself beat; Act 14's reset opening is echoed.
Chibiusa falls from the sky onto Usagi+Mamoru and demands the Silver Crystal = Act 14's ending into Act 15's opening, padded with an anime-original Koan fight.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 15 (loose: Black Moon vs Guardians over Chibiusa)
anchors.note: Spectre Sisters + Rubeus vs the five Guardians protecting Chibiusa parallels Act 15's Black Moon offensive; no abduction here (manga takes Mars).
Berthier's chess challenge to Ami = Act 16's Berthier/Mercury duel; anime skips Ami's abduction.
Rubeus abducts the four Guardians at once; the manga abducts Mars, Mercury, Jupiter across Acts 15-17 (they stay captive until Act 25).

anchors.chapters_adapted: 19 (partial: Sailor Pluto's debut, ahead of the time warp)
anchors.note: Pluto introduced (via Chibiusa/Luna-P) before the corridor journey; in the manga she debuts at the Space-Time Door in Act 19.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 19 (time warp, Space-Time Door, Pluto in person)
anchors.note: Party travels the corridor to the 30th century and meets Sailor Pluto at the Door = Act 19 in both summaries.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 20 (Crystal Tokyo, King Endymion, Chibiusa's parentage)-21 elements
anchors.note: King Endymion explains the Black Moon and reveals Chibiusa as Usagi+Mamoru's daughter; Demande covets Sailor Moon = Acts 20-21.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 22-23 (loose: Wiseman corrupts Chibiusa; Black Lady debuts)
anchors.note: Wiseman turns Chibiusa into Black Lady = Act 23's arrival of Black Lady (manga stages it on Nemesis; anime moves fast to the Dark Gate plot).
Finale: Death Phantom's full power vs Neo-Queen-empowered Sailor Moon; Chibiusa healed = Acts 24-26 compressed; manga's Sailor Chibi Moon debut and Sailor Pluto's death (Act 25) are omitted.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 27 (loose: omens of ruin, first Daimon fights, Uranus/Neptune glimpsed)
anchors.note: S opener = Act 27 Infinity 1 Premonition: apocalyptic vision, Daimon the inners can't beat, two mysterious new Guardians; anime re-stages the particulars.
Haruka introduced as an enigmatic 'boy', paired with Michiru = the mysterious pair the Guardians puzzle over in Acts 28-29.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 33 (Holy Grail; Super Sailor Moon's first transformation)
anchors.note: Sailor Moon becomes Super Sailor Moon via the Holy Grail = Act 33's exact beat; the grail's origin story differs (anime talisman quest is original).
Hotaru revealed as Sailor Saturn's vessel; outers resolve to kill her = Infinity's late-arc standoff (arc-span derivation, anime order differs).
Messiah of Silence awakens in Hotaru's body = Act 35's Mistress-9-awakens-Pharaoh-90 phase (arc-span derivation).
Hotaru expels Mistress 9, Sailor Saturn awakens, Pharaoh 90 finished = Acts 36-37's climax beats (talisman resonance vs anime's self-sacrifice staging).
Season close = Act 38 Infinite Journey epilogue: reborn baby Hotaru handed over, outers exit; anime adds the Uranus/Neptune challenge to Sailor Moon.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 39 (solar eclipse; Dead Moon Circus arrives; Pegasus meets Chibiusa in her dream)
anchors.note: SuperS opener = Act 39 Dream 1 Eclipse Dream beat for beat in both summaries.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 40-43 (motif condensation: the four inners' Super forms)
anchors.note: Mercury/Mars/Jupiter/Venus gain Super forms at once via Pegasus; the manga devotes one Dream act to each Guardian's own Sailor Crystal (Acts 40-43).
Pegasus's identity as Helios, guardian of the dream realm Elysion = Acts 43/46 exposition beats, heavily re-staged.
SuperS finale = Acts 48-49: Nehellenia beaten with the Golden Crystal's power; manga's Sailor Quartet awakening and outer-Guardian participation are absent.
Stars-arc adaptation starts here: Mamoru leaves for America (Galaxia takes his star seed in both - anime conceals it until ep 193) and the Three Lights arrive = Acts 50-51.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 51-53 elements (loose: outers' hard line against the Starlights)
anchors.note: Outer Guardians confront the Starlights' interference = the outers' independent plan of Acts 52-53 (arc-span derivation).
Mid-campaign checkpoint; Chibi Chibi's guardian turn loosely parallels Act 54's Sailor Chibi Chibi; anime order diverges.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 54 (Princess Kakyuu emerges from the incense burner)
anchors.note: Kakyuu's emergence and reunion with the Starlights = Act 54's Kakyuu beats; anime wraps it in the stolen-Silver-Crystal plot.
Inner Guardians eliminated by Galaxia; the manga staggers the Guardians' deaths across Acts 52-56 rather than one battle.
Final confrontation with Galaxia as Chaos's host, light-of-hope beat; the manga's Galaxy Cauldron setting and losses are absent.

continue_points.note: ep 60 only reaches Act 15's opening scenes - resume at Act 15 itself
Acts 40-43 are only echoed as a condensed motif; a reader should still read the four Dream acts in full

annotations.note: Rainbow Crystals / Seven Great Youma device is anime-original; manga's mid-arc (Tuxedo Mask broadcast, blackout, Silver Crystal race, Acts 6-9) only loosely echoed
brainwashed/ambiguous-Endymion phase stretches Act 11 Reunion - Endymion across the late season
Act 10 split: past-life memories surface in ep 35, the Moon-ruins visit with Queen Serenity is deferred to ep 44
the Guardians' deaths (ep 45) and Usagi's solo duel staging are anime-original; manga's Usagi-kills-Mamoru-and-herself beat is absent
Mamoru's visions/breakup subplot is an anime-original overlay across the Black Moon episodes
Spectre Sisters block: manga's serial abductions of Mars/Mercury/Jupiter condensed into one mass abduction (ep 73); anime redeems the sisters, manga kills them
Saphir's defection/death subplot is largely anime-original; the finale omits Sailor Chibi Moon's manga debut and Sailor Pluto's death (Act 25)
pure-heart crystals, the talisman hunt and the Grail quest are anime-original devices over Infinity's midsection (manga talismans are the outers' own weapons)
Chibiusa's return and Sailor Chibi Moon's presence sit at Black Moon's epilogue / Infinity's start in the manga; the anime defers them to mid-S
Hotaru is introduced at Infinity's opening in the manga, mid-season in the anime

dream-mirror victim-of-the-week structure is anime-original; the manga's per-senshi Dream acts (40-43) have no true episode counterparts, and the outer Guardians - central to the manga arc - never appear in SuperS
Diana's debut; the manga introduces her in 30th-century Crystal Tokyo during Black Moon
Amazon Trio endgame (humanity, sacrifice) is anime-original; the manga dispatches the Trio inside Acts 40-42
idol-life / Animamates-of-the-week structure is anime-original; only landmark beats track the manga

anime replaces the manga's Galaxy Cauldron journey (Sagittarius Zero Star, Lethe/Mnemosyne, Chaos, Sailor Cosmos) with an Earth-bound finale; deaths compressed and reordered; Chibi Chibi's identity changed (manga: Sailor Cosmos guise; anime: Galaxia's star seed / light of hope)

type_corrections.note: Nehelenia-revival arc is an anime-original continuation of SuperS's villain (Wikipedia: 'anime-original storyline'; fandom season page: continues the 4th season's story; manga Acts 50-52 open the Stars arc with Mamoru's departure and the Starlights - no Nehelenia revival). AFL's 'Manga Canon' typing here is wrong - a concrete AFL discredit instance.

structure.notes: NUMBERING: our chapter space 1-60 = the unified 'renewal' act numbering (introduced with the 2003-04 shinsoban, kept by kanzenban/Eternal/Kodansha USA, used by en-Wikipedia's chapter list and sailormoon.fandom.com) - identity mapping to our chapters, so no conversion was needed for any source used here. The original 1992-97 tankobon numbered the same content as 52 acts (8 long acts later split, e.g. original Act 24 = renewal Act 27); beware old sources (WikiMoon-era) that still use 52-act numbers. ARC SPANS (renewal numbering): Dark Kingdom 1-14, Black Moon 15-26, Infinity 27-38, Dream 39-49, Stars 50-60. SEASON MAP: S1 eps 1-46 <- Dark Kingdom; R eps 47-89 (47-59 anime-original Makai Tree, 60-88 <- Black Moon, 89 filler); S eps 90-127 <- Infinity; SuperS eps 128-166 <- Dream; Stars eps 167-200 (167-172 anime-original Nehelenia revival, 173-200 <- Stars). VOLUMES: our volume_boundaries follow the ORIGINAL 18-volume packaging carrying renewal act numbers (per en-WP chapter list): v1 1-5, v2 6-9, v3 10-13, v4 14-17, v5 18-20, v6 21-24, v7 25-27, v8 28-31, v9 32-35, v10 36-38, v11 side stories only (no mainline acts - MU's 'skips Vol 11' note), v12 39-41, v13 42-43 (+3 side stories), v14 44-46, v15 47-49, v16 50-52, v17 53-55, v18 56-60. STRUCTURE VERDICT: no per-episode chapter source exists for this show; the anime is a loose-parallel adaptation everywhere except the landmark beats anchored above, so chapter-level interpolation between checkpoints is unreliable mid-season (worst: S1 25-43, R 61-81, S 94-110, SuperS 129-163, Stars 174-192). The checkpoint lattice + annotations is the honest ceiling of precision; do not present interpolated per-episode chapter numbers as exact for this title.
